# Herdr Config Location and Example

## Config File Path

According to the documentation, the configuration file location depends on your operating system:

- **Linux and macOS:** `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`
- **Windows:** `%APPDATA%\herdr\config.toml`

You can verify the resolved path for your system by running `herdr --help`.

## Minimal Example Configuration

Here's a practical starter configuration with commonly-used keybindings:

```toml
onboarding = false

[keys]
prefix = "ctrl+b"
new_tab = "prefix+c"
next_tab = "prefix+n"
previous_tab = "prefix+p"
focus_pane_left = "prefix+h"
focus_pane_down = "prefix+j"
focus_pane_up = "prefix+k"
focus_pane_right = "prefix+l"
split_horizontal = "prefix+minus"
split_vertical = "prefix+pipe"

[terminal]
default_shell = "bash"

[theme]
name = "catppuccin"

[ui]
pane_borders = "auto"
```

This configuration sets up a tmux-like prefix mode using Ctrl+B, establishes vim-style navigation, applies the Catppuccin color scheme, and disables first-run onboarding.

Herdr is wired in. The `sme@generic` config evaluates and the dry-run build plans correctly. I didn't run `make switch` or build for the other hosts.

- **`flake.nix`**: added `herdr.url = "github:herdrdev/herdr/v0.9.3"`. The lock resolves to `7b116c0`, which is the tag's commit.
- **`home/sme/shared/base.nix`**: added `inputs` to the module args. The Herdr package is appended to `home.packages` as `inputs.herdr.packages.${pkgs.stdenv.hostPlatform.system}.default`, and `xdg.configFile."herdr/config.toml".source` points at the new file. All hosts already pass `inputs`.
- **`home/sme/shared/includes/herdr.toml`**: new file, staged because flakes ignore untracked files. `flake.lock` is also updated but not staged.

- **Config contents:** you had no existing Herdr config, so I wrote a starter from its docs: tmux-style `ctrl+b` prefix, vim-style pane focus, catppuccin theme, onboarding off. I didn't validate it against the config reference. Edit it to taste.
- **Path:** your note said `shared/includes/`. The real path is `home/sme/shared/includes/`.
- **nixpkgs:** Herdr uses its own nixpkgs and rust-overlay, which adds a second nixpkgs to the lock. Adding `herdr.inputs.nixpkgs.follows = "nixpkgs"` would dedupe it. I left it out because it could break their pinned Rust toolchain.
- **Build cost:** Herdr builds from source with Rust, so the first `make switch` will compile it.
- **Hosts:** `base.nix` is shared, so every host gets it. If you only want Herdr on some hosts, move it into per-host config.

# Target: herdr v0.9.3. Invalid keys fall back to defaults with a startup

name = "dracula"                      # built-in; replaces the dracula tmux plugin

[terminal]
new_cwd = "follow"

[ui]
tab_bar_position = "bottom"           # tmux status line position
prompt_new_tab_name = false           # tmux `c` doesn't prompt
pane_gaps = false                     # tmux-style shared dividers
pane_outer_borders = false
show_agent_labels_on_pane_borders = true
window_title = "{terminal_title} / {tab}"   # set-titles-string "#T / #W"

  { type = "zoom" },
  { type = "datetime", format = "%H:%M" },  # clock24 + @dracula-plugins "time"

[ui.toast]

[keys]
prefix = "ctrl+j"                     # programs.tmux.shortcut = "j"
detach = "prefix+d"                   # tmux default (herdr default is q)

# Already identical to tmux/herdr defaults, listed for clarity:
#   c new tab, x close pane, z zoom, [ copy mode, 1..9 tabs,
#   h/j/k/l focus panes (pain-control), R reload config

# pain-control splits: | and \ side-by-side, - and _ stacked
split_vertical   = ["prefix+|", "prefix+backslash", "prefix+v"]
split_horizontal = ["prefix+minus", "prefix+_"]

# pain-control H/J/K/L resize. Herdr puts swap on these by default, so move swap.
resize_pane_left  = "prefix+shift+h"
resize_pane_down  = "prefix+shift+j"
resize_pane_up    = "prefix+shift+k"

next_tab     = ["prefix+ctrl+l", "prefix+n"]

# bind Tab last-window. Herdr's last_pane crosses tabs and workspaces.
last_pane           = "prefix+tab"

cycle_pane_previous = "prefix+alt+space"

result.output:
# Herdr Configuration Extraction

## (1) Keybinding String Syntax Rules

Valid key syntax includes:
- Plain keys: `n`, `enter`, `tab`, `esc`, `left`, `right`, `up`, `down`
- Modifiers: `ctrl+a`, `shift+n`, `alt+1`, `cmd+k`
- Named punctuation: `minus`, `comma`, `ampersand`, `plus`, `backtick`
- Prefix mode: `prefix+n`
- Arrays for multiple shortcuts: `["prefix+n", "ctrl+alt+]"]`

The docs warn: *"Plain direct printable keys such as `n` are unsafe because they intercept typing; use `prefix+n` unless you intentionally want a direct binding."*

Navigate-mode keys (`navigate_workspace_*`, `navigate_pane_*`) may use plain keys like `j` or `k` but *"must not use `prefix+`, `esc`, `enter`, `tab`, `shift+tab`, `left`, `right`, or unmodified `1` through `9`."*

## (2) Built-in Theme Names

The docs state: *"Search `theme.name` in the Config reference for every built-in theme."* Specific examples mentioned include:
- `catppuccin`, `catppuccin-latte`
- `tokyo-night`, `tokyo-night-day`
- `gruvbox`, `gruvbox-light`
- `terminal` (follows host ANSI palette)

Dracula is not explicitly listed in this excerpt.

## (3) ui.window_title Placeholder Tokens

Valid tokens are: `{hostname}`, `{workspace}`, `{tab}`, `{pane}` (manual pane name), and `{terminal_title}` (focused pane's terminal title with spinners stripped). The docs note: *"Write `{{` and `}}` for literal braces. A token with no value renders empty."*

## (4) ui.tab_bar_right Item Syntax

Status area items include:
- `{ type = "zoom" }` — shows fixed `ZOOM` pill when zoomed
- `{ type = "hostname" }`
- `{ type = "datetime", format = "%H:%M" }` — uses `strftime` formatting
- `{ type = "text", text = "prod" }`
- `{ type = "command", command = "~/.config/herdr/status.sh", interval_seconds = 5, timeout_seconds = 2 }`

Command entries support `interval_seconds` (1–31,536,000) and `timeout_seconds` (1–3,600).

## (5) [[keys.command]] Syntax

Required and optional fields:
- `key` — keybinding string (required)
- `type` — required; valid types: `"popup"`, `"pane"`, `"shell"`, `"plugin_action"`
- `command` — command to run (required)
- `description` — optional; appears in help panel
- `width`, `height` — optional popup dimensions (terminal cells or percentages like `"80%"`)

Environment variables provided: *"`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `HERDR_BIN_PATH`, `HERDR_ACTIVE_WORKSPACE_ID`, `HERDR_ACTIVE_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, and `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` when those values are available."*

On Windows: *"custom command strings use `cmd.exe /d /c`, so environment variables use `%HERDR_BIN_PATH%` syntax."*

## (6) Invalid Keys Behavior

The docs state: *"If a config value is invalid, Herdr falls back to a safe default and shows a startup warning."* Invalid keybinding entries are rejected during config load; the system gracefully degrades rather than crashing.

content.text:
Herdr now follows the repo's module pattern, and your config is in use. It evaluates and dry-run builds on generic, ubuntu and bluestreak. Galvatron evaluates with the module enabled and the default opener (`xdg-open`). I haven't run `make switch`.

- **Your file:** the root `herdr.toml` moved to `home/sme/shared/includes/herdr.toml`, and the root copy is deleted. It is unchanged except for the URL popup.
- **URL popup:** `xargs -r open` is now `xargs -r @opener@`, and a comment above the popup says where the placeholder gets filled in.
- **New module `modules/home-manager/herdr.nix`:**
  - **Options:** it provides `webframp.herdr.enable` and `webframp.herdr.urlOpener`. The opener defaults to `open` on macOS and `xdg-open` on Linux. Bluestreak gets `open`.
  - **What it does:** it installs the Herdr package from the flake input and writes `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` with the opener filled in.
- **Wiring:** the module is registered in `default.nix`, imported in `base.nix`, and enabled there. My earlier inline wiring in `base.nix` is removed.
- **Unchanged:** the `herdr` flake input and `flake.lock` entries from before are as they were.

**Needs your input**
- **WSL opener:** on the WSL hosts, `xdg-open` only works if a browser handler is set up. To use `wslview`, set `webframp.herdr.urlOpener = "wslview";` in the host file. It needs `wslu` installed, and nothing in the repo installs it today.
- **Staging:** the new files are staged, and `flake.lock` and `flake.nix` are modified but unstaged. Nothing is committed.
